code: set.seed(1) n <- 1000 sim <- data.frame(   x1 = runif(n, -1, 1),   x2 = runif(n, -1, 1),   x3 = runif(n, -1, 1),   x4 = runif(n, -1, 1) ) true_effects <- list(   x1 = function(x) sin(pi * x),   x2 = function(x) 2 * (x^2 - 1 / 3),   x3 = function(x) x / 2 ) sim$y <- 1 +   true_effects$x1(sim$x1) +   true_effects$x2(sim$x2) +   true_effects$x3(sim$x3) +   2 * sim$x1 * sim$x2 +   rnorm(n, sd = 0.3) model <- rpf(y ~ ., data = sim, nthreads = 2) model #> ── Random Planted Forest model ───────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Regression. Prediction = intercept + the sum of 4 components. #> Intercept: 0.998346 #>  #> Components (largest first), importance = share of the variance of the prediction on the training rows: #>  component importance #>  x1:x2     34%        #>  x1        34%        #>  x2        26%        #>  x3        5.4%       #>  #> How it was chosen: #>   The forest: 200 tree families of 84 splits (chosen out of bag; growing stopped at 168). #>   From the forest's 14 nonzero components (purified): those with a share of at least 3% of the forest's Var(prediction), each with one coefficient, fitted out of bag (rule R). #>   Rule and threshold chosen by out-of-bag error (1-SE rule; 5 folds, seed 1954012425) among 16 candidates. #>   Left out: 10 components, shares together 0.19% (largest x1:x3, 0.054%). names(predict_components(model, new_data = sim)$m) #> [1] "x1"    "x2"    "x3"    "x1:x2" predict(model, new_data = head(sim)) #> # A tibble: 6 × 1 #>     .pred #>     <dbl> #> 1 -0.326  #> 2  0.0131 #> 3  1.17   #> 4  4.00   #> 5  1.17   #> 6  0.831 rpfit <- rpf(y ~ ., data = sim, max_interaction = 2, n_families = 50, prune = FALSE) rpfit #> ── Regression Random Planted Forest ──────────────────────────────────────────── #> Formula: `y ~ .` #> 50 tree families with 141 splits each on 4 predictors, interactions to degree #> 2. #> ℹ `n_splits` chosen out of bag (lowest corrected OOB RMSE 0.3359); growing stopped at #> 141 splits. #> ℹ Forest is not purified. #>  #> ── Tree growing  #>      split_structure: leaf #>   n_try_split_points: 3 #>     share_candidates: 0.1 #>       max_candidates: 50 #>     split_decay_rate: 0.1 #>        delete_leaves: TRUE #>  #> ℹ Fit using 1 thread, also the default for `predict()` and `purify()`.

title: Random Planted Forest: A Directly Interpretable Tree Ensemble
text: randomPlantedForest implements Random Planted Forest (Hiabu, Mammen & Meyer), tree ensemble whose predictions can read directly, without post-hoc explanation methods. Like random forest, averages many tree-based models grown bootstrap samples. Unlike random forest, models sum trees split fixed set predictors, max_interaction bounds many predictors can . max_interaction = 1 forest additive model; 2 adds pairwise interactions, . result, fitted model decomposes exactly intercept, main effects interactions order: m̂(x)=m̂0+∑km̂k(xk)+∑k<lm̂kl(xk,xl)+…\hat m(x) = \hat m_0 + \sum_k \hat m_k(x_k) + \sum_{k < l} \hat m_{kl}(x_k, x_l) + \dots component can inspected plotted , together sum prediction. default rpf() fits three-way interactions, chooses number splits bag forest grows, leaves components small matter, returns sparse final model (prune = FALSE returns whole forest).
